definition.text: Maximum economic yield (MEY) is the level of catch that gives society the largest net economic benefit, or profit, from a fishery.

facts.text: Like optimum sustainable yield, it is a harvest rate below maximum sustainable yield.
At MEY the resource rent is at its maximum.
In bioeconomic terms, a fishery is overfished when catches exceed MEY.
A profit-maximising owner fishes until marginal revenue equals marginal cost, the condition the Gordon-Schaefer model uses.

definition.text: Surplus production models are the simplest of the three common kinds of fish stock assessment model, needing the least data.

facts.text: Schaefer's version, based on Verhulst's logistic growth, uses the catch equation H = qEX, linking catch to fishing effort and stock biomass.
Setting catch equal to natural growth gives an equilibrium catch for each long-run level of fishing effort.
These models, which estimate MSY directly, made MSY popular in the 1950s.

definition.text: Fishing effort is the amount of human work put into catching fish; excess effort and overcapacity in fishing fleets threaten the sustainability of fish stocks.

facts.text: A good effort measure is roughly proportional to the catch, for example a trawl fleet's engine power times days at sea (kW × days).
Global landings peaked in the late 1980s and are declining despite rising fishing effort.
Some fisheries subsidies encourage overcapacity and excess effort; WTO members agreed to ban certain such subsidies.
Schaefer assumed that in an unregulated fishery effort rises until no more profit can be made.

definition.text: Optimal harvesting theory uses optimisation methods from economics and operations research to choose the best rate and timing of harvest, and is widely used in fisheries.

facts.text: Population dynamics is the basis for working out optimal harvesting rates.
Economically, the aim is to maximise the present value of all future profits from the resource.
If density dependence acts only on larvae, the optimum is to harvest a single most valuable life stage at MSY.
Faustmann's formula applies the same logic to forests, giving the best harvest age from growth, timber prices and a discount rate.
